task: PR #1191's named next lever / decode-compiler-tree-witness-search-cost-finding.json next_steps[0]: hoist the @lru_cache-wrapped _tail closure (pack.py:402) out of the per-top-level-candidate loop in _openui_completion_domain so sibling candidates share witness-search results, with a unit test proving witness content and nodes_left fairness are unchanged, then re-measure compiler_ms/_sync-call-count.
change_summary: Moved the @lru_cache-wrapped _tail function (and its nodes_left fairness-budget box) from being constructed fresh inside _tail_from (called once per non-EOS top-level candidate) to being constructed once per _openui_completion_domain call, before the candidate loop. _tail_from now just resets a shared _nodes_left[0]=16 counter per call and reuses the shared _tail. lru_cache maxsize changed 64 -> None (unbounded within one call's lifetime).
safety_argument: _build_openui_completion_forest's result for a given (current, room) key depends only on request.tokenizer/slot_contract/max_path_tokens/min_content, all constant across the whole call, never candidate-specific. nodes_left gates whether the function BODY runs at all; a cache hit skips the body entirely, so widening cache scope can only ever grant a free win on an already-proven state, never cost a candidate a real chance.

answer: Hoisting the _tail lru_cache out of the per-candidate loop is safe (byte-identical witness content, unchanged coverage/n_paths, preserved nodes_left fairness) and structurally verified (cache-object count collapses from 2/14 to 1/1). It does NOT reduce _sync/compiler_ms on either measured prefix: cache_info shows 0 hits both before and after (22 and 4419 misses respectively, 0 hits in both scopes) because the (current, room) key is an absolute, strictly-monotonic token-id history + remaining-budget pair that structurally cannot collide -- neither across sibling candidates nor within one candidate's own recursion. The predecessor finding's premise (sibling candidates re-explore identical grammar states) does not hold for this cache's key shape.
